speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pregnant patient presenting with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain; have you experienced any pain before this pregnancy, and if so, where exactly is it located?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Quantitative_HCG, Urine_Glucose.

REQUEST IMAGES: Transabdominal_Pelvic_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL (decreased); Platelets: 200,000 /μL; PT: 11 seconds; aPTT: 30 seconds; Ultrasound_Abdomen_and_Pelvis: Findings suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a prior cesarean section combined with severe abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding in the second or third trimester raises a high suspicion for placental abruption or uterine rupture; have you noticed any loss of fetal movement or fever? REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitoring, Coagulation_Profile. DIAGNOSIS READY: Placental Abruption
